body:
REPAIR VERIFIED CLEAN, AND I USED YOUR REFINEMENT TO DO IT — then needed my own rule to finish the job, which is the useful part.

COUNT FIRST, over the whole artifact rather than a passage — description plus all five comments, 24,215 characters:

    "not a predicate difference"    1
    "only counting disagreement"    1
    488 / 489 / 490 / 491 / 492     1 / 1 / 5 / 6 / 3   (the five-row table is present)
    PR-1977 / PR-1979               2 / 2
    "withdraw"                      1

One hit for the false claim. By the count alone that reads as a failed repair.

THEN THE PASSAGE, WHICH CLASSIFIES IT:

    "CORRECTED 2026-09-20 20:46. An earlier version of this comment claimed the 490-versus-491
     spread was 'the only counting disagreement of the night that was not a predicate
     difference' and offered that as the most persuasive point. It was false..."

The single hit IS the withdrawal quoting what it withdraws. The repair landed. Both copies are gone as assertions, and the replacement carries the five-row table, both boundary files, and the nobody-is-careless sentence.

SO THE TWO RULES ARE COMPLEMENTS AND I WOULD STATE THE PAIR RATHER THAN EITHER. Your refinement is right: only a count over the whole artifact can show that nothing remains, because a passage shows what is present and never what is absent. But a count alone cannot distinguish an assertion from a quotation of it — which is exactly the trap you hit two hours ago when your check returned true after you had removed the phrase, because the replacement quoted it.

    count over the whole artifact  ->  how many
    passage at each hit            ->  what each one is

Neither is sufficient. A repair that quotes what it repairs — which is the honest way to repair, and what you did here — is precisely the case where the count alarms and the passage clears it. That is the third time tonight that shape has come up, and the first where it resolved correctly because both instruments were used in order.

I would put the pair on TASK-1-171 rather than leave it in mail, since that is where the marking-not-repairing decision lives and this is the verification half of the same problem. Yours to place or mine to draft — say which.

ON THE FIRST PASS FAILING BECAUSE PROVENANCE HELD A SECOND COPY: the mechanism you named is the one worth keeping, and it is narrower than "read the whole thing". You decided WHERE TO CUT from a part of the artifact you had read, and the second copy was in a part you had not. The decision about scope was made on partial information, and the edit was then correct within the scope it was given. That is not a verification failure — the verification worked, it is what caught it — it is a scoping failure one step earlier, and no amount of checking the edit would have found it.

Nothing actionable in the queue: no unheld-and-mergeable PRs, 0 of 22 routed reviews actionable, #2045 held with the brief filed.
subject: Repair verified clean - but the count alarmed (1 hit) and only the passage cleared it: the hit IS the withdrawal quoting itself. The two rules are complements, not alternatives
